results.invariant: At-least-once delivery does not execute the same command twice.
A released or recovered old Worker cannot reuse an obsolete ExecutionGrant.
A stale Worker cannot cross the transaction-scoped ExecutionGrant boundary into browser-visible JetStream events.
At-least-once Session mutation delivery creates one canonical PostgreSQL effect.
A replacement Worker crosses the Session-keyed projection barrier and rechecks its ExecutionGrant before reading PostgreSQL.
A streaming-path failure cannot roll back a complete Pi message already committed to SessionStorage.
A browser-visible failed prefix remains model-visible after Worker replacement.
A successful Run terminal commit does not reconstruct a complete message from the short-lived delta tail.
A JetStream event watermark already ahead of the Worker ACK cannot strand terminal Run settlement.
A Control Plane process replacement does not revoke a healthy Agent Loop's ExecutionGrant.
A stale Control Channel cannot retire a Worker whose active RunAttempt still has fresh database authority.
After connection and ExecutionGrant expiry, a dead management endpoint cannot strand the interrupted Run or Session.
Worker loss settles its model reservation so the replacement Run does not wait for quota TTL.
A replacement writer can retire a failed activation, while a revoked ExecutionGrant cannot start another Tool operation.
Checkpoint integrity and compare-and-swap generation checks survive cold recovery.
Exactly one terminal Run outcome wins a cancel/complete race.
A superseded dispatcher cannot start external work.
Expired ownership is reconciled only after the orphan runtime is terminated.
